reported.title: No under-temperature fault handling; cold probe opens the gas valve
reported.description: The control logic in loop() only checks the lockout key (line 57-62) and the 70/75 °C hysteresis band (lines 63-70); there is no branch for tempC < 5.0 °C, so a cold reading falls into the `tempC < FIRE_ON_C` branch at line 63 and calls setValve(true) at line 65, opening the valve. Measured evidence confirms this: in the 'Cold fault below 5 C' scenario D6 was not LOW for 1540 ms (allowed 500 ms), and with a disconnected probe (0 V) D6 stayed non-LOW for 5500 ms. The same missing guard means rail-to-rail readings also fail (3500 ms non-LOW). During the fault, D6 was not in safe state LOW for 5500 ms (allowed 500 ms to react).

judge_input.spec:
- Boiler probe on A1 at 10 mV/°C; gas valve on D6; lockout key on D3 (pull-up, active LOW).
- Open the valve (HIGH) when temperature is below 70.0 °C; close the valve when temperature is above 75.0 °C.
- If temperature reads above 120.0 °C or below 5.0 °C, force the valve CLOSED (LOW) within 500 ms.
- While D3 is held LOW, keep the valve CLOSED.
- Print `boiler: <temp> C valve=OPEN` or `boiler: <temp> C valve=SHUT` every 1000 ms.
- Reach the commanded valve state within 500 ms of a sustained in-range band crossing.
